judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Class-1 Content statements with resolved coordinate rank 0 under the same Curricular Goal CG-1 ('Children make sense of their surroundings through mathematics using numbers... develop a sense of quantity'), but under different competencies: the first under C-1.7 (represent numbers using place value, read numbers and number names) with LCs 'Read numbers up to 50' and 'Write numbers up to 50'; the second under C-1.8 (develop and use strategies for addition/subtraction) with LC 'Use strategies to subtract numbers up to 20'. These are complementary Class-1 number strands: symbolic reading and writing of numerals across a range that contains the subtraction range reinforces and is applied alongside subtraction computation within the same class, which is substantive pair-specific instructional coherence beyond the generic nomination tokens ('to', 'up', 'numbers'), the shared CG-1 ancestor, the weak rank_gap-0 proximity, and same-page proximity. No developmental direction is supported: at identical rank 0 the evidence shows parallel strands rather than the deepening, extension, or increased complexity of the same capability that a same-rank buildsTowards would require, and the second statement's text and LC make no reference to written recording of numerals. Judgment is therefore the symmetric relatesTo with null direction, in canonical endpoint order. Confidence is moderated because both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (32 and 24 omitted items) and all endpoints and ancestors carry upstream merge/audit context, with the competencies and curricular goal lacking developmental coordinates.

judgment.rationale: Both are Class-2 Content statements (same canonical coordinate rank 1) under Competency C-1.3 (grouping objects by attributes) within CG-1. The first concerns generating 2-D shapes from 3-D objects via shadows, impressions and tracing (LCs: form 2-D shapes using tracing/shadows/impressions); the second concerns classifying 2-D shapes by properties such as sides and corners (LC: classify 2-D shapes by number of sides and corners). They share the 2-D shape object of study and are mutually reinforcing — hands-on shape formation supplies shapes whose attributes can be examined — but the evidence shows two complementary activities (physical generation vs. property-based classification) at the same class level with no source-backed statement that one is required for or substantively extends the other, so same-rank developmental direction is not warranted. Endpoint text and LCs are trustworthy, though both SFIs carry merge/duplicate-extraction audit context and truncated source evidence (34 omitted items each), limiting how much additional sequencing evidence could be assessed; the parent Competency and Curricular Goal lack developmental coordinates and were used as context only.

judgment.rationale: Both are Content SFIs under Competency C-3.3 (recognizes and creates symmetry, including reflection and rotation) within CG-3. The second SFI (Class-4, rank 3) is concrete recognition/creation of symmetrical shapes via paper folding and mirror (LCs: recognise and create symmetrical shapes through paper folding; using a mirror), i.e., hands-on establishment of reflection symmetry. The first SFI (Class-5, rank 4) extends this to generating patterns using both reflection and rotation symmetry (LCs: create patterns using reflection symmetry; using rotation symmetry), adding the rotation transformation and a productive pattern-generation demand. Proficiency with the Class-4 concrete reflection work supports success in the Class-5 pattern creation, so the lower-rank Class-4 item builds towards the higher-rank Class-5 item; this is substantive extension rather than generic repetition. Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (32 omitted items each) and both endpoints and ancestors carry merge/audit context (duplicate-window extractions), which does not alter the shared-competency text used here.

judgment.rationale: Both are Content SFIs under the same Competency C-4.4 ('Develops strategies to estimate time') within CG-4 measurement. The first (Class-4, rank 3) is 'Solve problems involving time in daily life contexts using addition and subtraction', with LCs for adding and subtracting time in daily-life word problems; the second (Class-5, rank 4) is 'Time duration in hours and minutes', with an LC 'Estimate time duration in hours and minutes'. Additive/subtractive reasoning with clock time in daily contexts is precisely the computational basis for determining and estimating elapsed duration in hours and minutes, so proficiency in the Class-4 content supports success in the Class-5 duration work; direction is lower-to-higher rank, which is the only permitted buildsTowards direction. This is substantive extension (from operating on given times to quantifying/estimating duration), not mere shared 'time' wording. Both endpoints carry upstream audit/merge context and truncated source evidence, and the shared ancestors lack developmental coordinates, so the judgment rests only on the bounded resolved Content text, coordinates, and LCs.
